themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about cannabis retailers in CD 201 surged to 3 this week, a 500% spike above the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling potential unlicensed or non-compliant retail operations emerging in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Spike timing: emerged in current week only, no pattern in prior weeks
High statistical severity classification despite lower z-score relative to other spikes
reporting_angles: Are these complaints targeting unlicensed or illegal retailers, or regulated shops with operational issues?
Interview neighbors and local merchants about where these retailers are located and what specific violations are being reported

themes_detail.label: Drinking/Public Intoxication Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Drinking complaints in CD 201 exploded to 4 last week, a 967% increase from the 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score 7.49), representing the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting a severe public drinking/intoxication problem has emerged.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike, highest z-score at 7.49)
Represents the single most statistically severe anomaly across all complaint categories
Aligns with community board budget requests for homeless services, suggesting intersection of homelessness and public drinking
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints to identify if they cluster in specific blocks or transit hubs; interview NYPD and local precinct about enforcement patterns
Profile the connection between encampment surge (11 complaints last week, up 389%) and drinking complaints—are these linked phenomena?
Speak with residents and business owners in affected blocks about safety impacts and whether this is new or long-standing

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge in Mott Haven
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints spiked to 11 last week, a 389% increase from the 2.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score 4.72), indicating a rapid deterioration in unsheltered homelessness visible on streets in CD 201.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average (389% spike, z-score 4.72)
Converges with community board's repeated funding requests for homeless services (01 budget request over multiple years)
Correlates temporally with drinking complaint spike (4 last week), suggesting possible comorbidity
reporting_angles: Locate and photograph the 11 encampments reported last week; interview residents about their needs and access to shelters
Contact NYC Department of Homeless Services to determine shelter capacity in/near CD 201 and why encampments are growing
Interview community board members about why homeless services remain an unfunded priority year after year

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints in CD 201 jumped to 11 this week, a 487% spike from the 1.9 weekly average, paired with a related root/sewer/sidewalk condition spike 3 weeks ago (5 complaints, up 1233%), indicating sanitation department service failures are accumulating.
evidence: 11 street sweeping complaints this week vs. 1.9 weekly average (487% spike, z-score 4.5)
Related spike: root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints peaked at 5 three weeks ago (1233% spike, z-score 6.65)
Sanitation worker complaint spike 2 weeks ago (3 complaints, 1100% increase) suggests possible staffing or route changes
reporting_angles: Request DSNY schedule and staffing data for CD 201 to determine if routes were cut or consolidated recently
Walk affected blocks to document visible trash accumulation and ask residents how long conditions have been poor
Interview DSNY about the sanitation worker complaints filed 2 weeks ago—were there labor disputes or route closures?

themes_detail.label: Lead Hazard Complaints Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in CD 201 spiked to 3 two weeks ago, a 700% increase from the 0.4 weekly average (z-score 5.42), a critical public health signal in a historically high-lead housing stock, particularly given ongoing building permits (420 filed in 90 days, 291 alterations).
evidence: 3 lead complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
420 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (291 alterations) suggest active renovation work that may be disturbing lead paint
Community board requests additional building inspectors repeatedly, indicating capacity gaps in oversight
reporting_angles: Obtain the 3 lead complaint details: which buildings, what type of lead hazard, were they tied to renovation work?
Interview HPD about lead inspection capacity and whether the recent permit surge has outpaced inspector availability
Investigate whether lead disclosure and containment protocols are being followed during the 291 active alterations; speak with residents in those buildings
